h1_living_vs_fast_food.interpretation: Living arrangement creates highly statistically significant variance in fast food consumption (Hostelers consume significantly more fast food than students living with family).

h2_screen_vs_sleep.interpretation: Statistically significant moderate-to-strong negative correlation (r = -0.41), proving high screen exposure suppresses sleep duration.

h3_breakfast_vs_energy.interpretation: Breakfast eaters report significantly higher mean energy (8.1/10) compared to habitual skippers (6.3/10).

h4_barrier_vs_risk.interpretation: Perceived barriers (especially lack of time and food delivery access) are significantly associated with high-risk lifestyle clustering.

key_insights.title: The Hostel Fast-Food Trap
key_insights.detail: Hostel and dormitory residents consume fast food an average of 3.9 days/week, compared to only 0.9 days/week for those living with parents (ANOVA F = 272.7, p < 0.001). Lack of kitchen access and late-night food delivery are the primary drivers.

key_insights.title: The Blue-Light Sleep Debt Crisis
key_insights.detail: 90.5% of young adults sleep less than the recommended 7 hours per night. Every 2 additional hours of recreational screen time is associated with approximately 0.72 hours of lost sleep (r = -0.41, p < 0.001).

key_insights.title: Breakfast Omission Drains Cognitive Vitality
key_insights.detail: Young adults skipping breakfast show a 2.1-point drop in self-reported daily energy levels (6.3 vs 8.1 on a 10-point scale; t = 14.0, p < 0.001), which strongly correlates with midday fatigue and higher sugar cravings.

key_insights.title: Stress-Induced Dietary Dysregulation
key_insights.detail: Respondents experiencing high stress (>= 7/10) reported a 64% higher rate of intense sugar cravings and consumed 1.8 more fast food meals weekly than low-stress peers, indicating widespread emotional eating.

key_insights.title: The Sedentary Cascade on Metabolic Health
key_insights.detail: Young adults exercising under 2 hours per week combined with >= 4 days of fast food intake exhibited an average BMI of 24.8, placing 58.4% of them in the Overweight or Obese categories.

key_insights.title: Financial Burden of Convenience Foods
key_insights.detail: Frequent fast-food consumers spend an average of ₹5,008 monthly on food, which is 42% higher than students who cook at least 4 days a week (₹5,696), dispelling the myth that cooking is more expensive.
